headline: Distribution consolidators extend pricing power and margins through access control.

deltas.reads: Components and technology distribution accelerates sharply, showing channel control through the broadest demand recovery cycle.
Pharmaceutical and specialty solutions moat deepens, with segment profit up 18% despite tariff headwinds.
Healthcare distribution maintains recurring institutional demand, with specialty and services attachment lifting underlying dependence.
Regional landfill and collection density translates directly to sustained pricing power without erosion.
Technical distribution tightens lock-in as Engineered Solutions attachment and MRO dependence compound.
Broker as access layer extracts margin through pricing discipline independent of underlying freight demand.
Energy and PVF distribution reaches sufficient scale and density that customer switching costs cement durability.

momentum_note: The spread machine is visibly accelerating. Across these seven distributors, the pattern is consistent: pricing power is expanding even as growth moderates, access dependence is deepening through service attachment and technical capability, and the underlying commodity or throughput is increasingly secondary to the intermediary's control. Arrow's 32% growth shows recovery breadth; Cardinal and Cencora show pharmaceutical and healthcare system lock-in independent of headline volume; Casella, CHRW, and DNOW show that regional/sectoral density and pricing discipline matter more than commodity price movement; Applied shows technical services compounding the moat. This is not a cyclical recovery story. These are structurally entrenched intermediaries extending their spreads.
